jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher – Lipidomics and Fatty Acid Metabolism in Inflammation (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: ...you're in the middle of itThe Institute of Clinical Pharmacology at Goethe University Frankfurt is seeking a PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher to join the research group of Dr. Hahnefeld. The successful candidate will contribute to an interdisciplinary research project in cooperation with the Fraunhofer ITMP Frankfurt at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipid biology and inflammation research.The project investigates how lipid metabolism and lipid-mediated signaling are regulated in inflammatory settings. The work combines cell-based experiments with mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and targeted lipid mediator measurements. A particular focus will be placed on the development, optimization and application of robust analytical and computational workflows for the analysis of complex biological datasets. The research group uses high-resolution mass spectrometry and reproducible bioinformatic approaches to investigate lipid-mediated mechanisms in inflammatory and metabolic diseases. The position offers the opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment with interdisciplinary partners in lipid biology, immunology, imaging and proteomics.The position is limited up to three years.Your Role:- Plan, conduct and document experiments in cellular models of inflammation and metabolic perturbation.- Prepare biological samples and perform LC-HRMS-based lipidomics and metabolomics measurements and further develop associated analytical workflows.- Perform GC-HRMS-based analysis of fatty acids- Conduct LC-MS/MS measurements of lipid mediators using established methods.- Perform comprehensive quality control, raw-data validation, data annotation and statistical analysis of complex mass spectrometry datasets.- Develop and apply reproducible workflows for data processing, visualization and interpretation using R and/or Python.- Contribute to the integration and interpretation of lipidomics data with complementary datasets generated by collaborating groups, including imaging- and proteomics-based data.- Validate selected findings in close collaboration with project partners.- Present research results in scientific publications, project meetings and at national and international conferences.... your skills are what we're looking for- A completed Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in analytical chemistry, chemistry, pharmacy, biochemistry, molecular life sciences or a related discipline.- A strong theoretical and practical background in analytical chemistry.- Practical experience with liquid chromatography, gas chromatography and mass spectrometry is desirable.- Experience with high-resolution mass spectrometry, lipidomics, metabolomics, method development or biological sample preparation is advantageous but not necessary.- Experience in cell culture, molecular or cellular biology is advantageous.- Knowledge of statistical data analysis and programming in R and/or Python, or a strong willingness to acquire these skills.- A careful, structured and independent working style, combined with reliability and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team.- Very good written and spoken English skills.- Due to legal regulations, valid proof of measles immunity / measles vaccination is required... you'll be offered a lot- In addition to an attractive salary based on acollective agreement (TV-G-U, E 13)with an annual special payment, you benefit from long-term security through company pension schemes- An interdisciplinary doctoral research project at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipidomics and inflammation research.- Close scientific supervision and structured training in high-resolution mass spectrometry, lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and reproducible data analysis.- Remote Work possible- Benefit from our attractive health offers. We offer regular online and face-to-face courses on nutrition, relaxation, sports and exercise- Part-time employment is possible, we offer childcare in our daycare center (if you have any questions, please contact UKF-Familienservice), child care during holidays- Free public transport in all Hessen (Free State Ticket Hessen)- Uniklinik-Campus, Mensa, Cafés- Insights: Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn- FAQ´s for new employees**It's time to join our team! **Contact: Dr. Lisa Hahnefeld, Leader Research GroupEmail: hahnefeld@med.uni-frankfurt.de** **Application Deadline: 08.11.2026We welcome applications from candidates of all genders. Die Medizinische Hochschule Hannover (MHH), mit rund 10.000 Beschäftigten größter Landesbetrieb des Landes Niedersachsen, ist eine universitäre Einrichtung für Forschung und Lehre in der Human- und Zahnmedizin und ein Universitätsklinikum der Supramaximalversorgung. Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.About UsThe Hannover Medical School (MHH), with about 10,000 employees the biggest company of Lower Saxony, is a university institution for research and teaching in the human and dental medicine and a university hospital of supra-maximum medical care. Research, teaching, medical care and administration work hand in hand in the integration model at the MHH-campus.The Peter L. Reichertz Institute for Medical Informatics (PLRI) is one of the largest university centres for medical informatics in Germany. It belongs to two leading universities, is situated in one of Europe's most research-intensive regions, and offers excellent opportunities for research. In interdisciplinary projects, the PLRI collaborates with health centres, research institutes, corporations, and public institutions in order to shape the future of the health system and medicine. The activities range from diverse topics on the local level, to regional, national, and global collaborations.The research group "Clinical Data Science" focuses on the detection of novel routine clinical and -omics biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis to personalize and thus improve patient treatment. To achieve this, we integrate phenotypical information and routine clinical as well as (multi)-omics data by high-dimensional statistics and state-of-the-art artificial intelligence to gain novel insights into underlying disease pathomechanisms. Moreover, we are interested in developing and implementing research data platforms for complex (multi-)omics data. The project "MALDIDive: Enabling AI Research with Public MALDI-TOF Fingerprints across Microbial Diversity", to be carried out within an interdisciplinary research team and funded by the German Research Foundation, will establish a well curated data platform of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry datasets from the Leibniz Institute German Collection of Mircoorganisms and Cell Cultures GmbH (DSMZ). We are looking for an enthusiastic PostDoc who is interested in omics data platform development and deployment for future AI use.Your Responsibilities- data platform architecture, backend, and frontend development as well as deployment for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry database/platform and associated metadata- development of interactive data visualization concepts and their implementation into data platform- development and realization of short explanatory videos for platform users- co-organization and co-leading of stakeholder workshops to define user requirements and conduct user test cycles- presentation to the scientific community, i.e., by publishing in high-level journals and via presentations at international conferences- close collaboration with interdisciplinary project partners from AI / data science, analytical, and micro­biological research communities, particularly the DSMZ- bachelor / master student co-supervisionYour Profile- PhD / Dr. rer. nat. / Dr.-Ing. degree in data science / bioinformatics / computational biology / informatics / physics or similar research fields- expertise in the work on databases, interactive platform development, -omics and biomedical data, and / or artificial intelligence / machine learning- proficiency in backend / frontend development and / or database programming, including one or more of the following programming languages: VueJS, TypeScript, SQL, PYTHON, R Shiny, nginx, Docker, etc.- proficiency in English (written and oral)- desired: experience with code documentary systems and RestAPI- desired: knowledge of the German languageWe offer- a full-time position initially limited to two years with 38.5 hours per week at one of the largest employers in the state of Lower Saxony- depending on your individual qualifications, a salary according to TV-L salary group E13 is possible, with the benefits associated with public sector employment (e.g. occupational pension scheme and supplementary insurance through VBL)- an exciting role at the interface of research, healthcare and science management- a supportive induction process within a motivated and interdisciplinary team- support to pursue postdoctoral career (e.g., mentoring programs, etc.)- working in a highly motivated and cooperative research team of scientists- excellent perspectives for your scientific career development and jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.Your tasks- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.Your profile- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Hanieh Saeediat hanieh.saeedi@senckenberg.de

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its institute Senckenberg am Meer, German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research in Hamburg, starting as soon as possibleResearch Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity(full time / part-time )Location: HamburgEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options availableType of contract: temporary contract limited until 30.09.2029Remuneration: collective agreement of the state Hesse, TV-H E13﻿The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.As part of the institute “Senckenberg am Meer” located in Wilhelmshaven, with its two departments Marine Research and German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research (DZMB), the Hamburg research site, which belongs to the DZMB, focuses on researching taxonomy and systematics of marine life forms.The position is based within the Zooplankton Working Group and is part of the joint project ZooM-In (Innovative Methods for National Zooplankton Monitoring), contributing to the further development and standardization of modern methods for marine biodiversity monitoring. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) through the National Biodiversity Monitoring Centre’s initiative Sustainable Biodiversity Monitoring.The project will be carried out in close cooperation with the Helmholtz Institute for Functional Marine Biodiversity (HIFMB) as well as federal and state authorities.Your tasks- Project management of the project ZooM-In- Organisation of and participation in monthly expeditions (March-October, 3-4 days per months) to the North Sea- Organisation of project workshops- Assessment of zooplankton biodiversity by imaging technologies- Cross validation of zooplankton biodiversity assessment by traditional microscopy, molecular genetics and imaging methods- Communication of project results to stakeholders- Publication of project results in peer-reviewed journals- Writing of a project reportYour profile- Master degree in marine biology or natural sciences- Expertise in the application of plankton imaging technologies (ZooScan and/or PlanktoScope)- Relevant knowledge on molecular genetic analyses of organisms, ideally metabarcoding of zooplankton- Experience in data analyses, preferably using R- Experience with sea-going expeditions on research vessels and sampling of plankton, resilience to motion sickness- Willingness to participate in interdisciplinary work- Very good communication skills, ability to work in a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary and international environment- Very good command of English (written and spoken)- Sound command of the German language is essential for this positionWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan- Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) (as a single PDF, max. 10 MB) on our career pagehttps://www.senckenberg.de/de/karriere/ by 8 November 2026.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/.For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.If you have any specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Jasmin Renz at jasmin.renz@senckenberg.de.

With state-of-the-art technologies, a high degree of vertical integration and a clear vision for sustainable aviation, we are actively shaping the future.Since our foundation in 1999, we have grown steadily and now employ an international team of nearly 100 qualified specialists and engineers.
